summary: sqli.py is the opt-in (RECCE_ACTIVE_ATTACKS=1) active SQL injection tester — error-based, boolean-blind, time-based — plus a sqlmap orchestration hand-off. Everything is T1 (deterministic detection) except the sqlmap chain which reaches T2/T3 depending on what sqlmap dumps. Biggest gap: no automatic wiring from crawl.py's discovered params/forms; caller must invoke test_url_param / test_form by hand, and the sqlmap chain is not currently invoked from any scan runbook.

findings.tier_evidence: Single-quote injection triggers canonical DB error signature — deterministic, DB flavor identified.
findings.promotion_notes: With confirmed error-based, chain to UNION SELECT version(),user(),database() and record the returned strings → T2 data-extraction proof.

findings.tier_evidence: AND 1=1 vs AND 1=2 length delta >= 32 bytes reproducibly.
findings.promotion_notes: sqlmap --technique=B extracts row counts / schema — T2 data proof.

findings.tier_evidence: SLEEP payload consistently pushes response past baseline+N-margin.
findings.promotion_notes: sqlmap --technique=T extracts data byte-by-byte via time oracle.

findings.tier_evidence: sqlmap's Parameter/Type lines confirm injection; --dbs/--dump can extract data — T2 read proof, T3 if admin hash cracked.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain to hash cracking (hashcat -m 300 mysql, -m 1731 mssql) and OS shell via --os-shell / --os-pwn on MSSQL/PostgreSQL → T3 foothold.
